A1.1 Module 5 Session 3B — Production & Fluency 75–90 min
🎤 ⚔️ 🔗 🎧 🏆 5 badges · can / like / need · Full production 🎉 All 5 badges — S3B complete!
§1
Hot Take · Opinion Opener
Remember from S3A · Activate can / like / need · No notes · Full sentences
5–8 min
⚡ Teacher Note — S3B Opening
No grammar review. Jump straight into Hot Take. Say: "No notes today. You know this material. Every sentence you make uses can, like, or need. Let's go." S3B is 100% production. If a student reaches for notes — stop them. The discomfort is the learning.
Hot Take 1: "Saying 'Sure, no problem!' when you're not 100% sure is worse than saying nothing."
T–S · Stand up if you agree · Defend in 1 sentence using CAN or CAN'T
Hot Take 2: "Saying 'I'm not really into coffee' is more professional than 'I don't like coffee.'"
S–S · Debate with partner · Use: like / don't like / prefer in your argument
Hot Take 3: "When you say 'Can I get a coffee?', you're really asking for permission, not checking your own ability."
Class · Open debate · Who's right? Justify with grammar + example from real life
8 min · 3 hot takes · Badge b1 · Every student speaks at least once
§2
Pitch & Debate Round
Role-play scenarios · Full production of can / like / need · S–S + T–S
12–15 min
⚡ Teacher Note — Pitch Round
Each scenario forces students to produce can/like/need under real conversational pressure. Your job: play the skeptical interviewer or client. Push back after every answer. Target: 6+ correct uses of can/like/need per student per scenario. Count and announce the score.
🎯 Scenario 1 — The Job Interview (T–S)
Teacher plays HR manager at Vertex Logistics, Celaya. Student is the candidate. Question: "Tell me what you can do for this company, what you like about logistics work, and what you need from us to do your best job."

Student has 90 seconds to answer — no notes.
Must include: 2 things you CAN do · 1 thing you CAN'T do yet (honest!) · 1 thing you LIKE about the work · 1 thing you NEED from the company
⚔️ Scenario 2 — Skills Debate (S–S)
Partner A thinks soft skills (like communication and teamwork) are more important for a job. Partner B thinks technical skills (like Excel, SAP, or machinery) are more important. Debate for 2 minutes — each must use CAN at least 3 times and LIKE at least once.
SOFT SKILLS — Communication side
💡 "I can communicate with any client — that's the real skill."
💡 "A machine can do Excel — a person can build a relationship."
💡 "I like working with people — machines don't motivate a team."
TECHNICAL SKILLS — Tools side
💡 "I can use SAP and Excel — that saves 3 hours per day."
💡 "You can like your team but you need real skills to deliver."
💡 "I can fix the system when it breaks — can your communicator?"
🤝 Scenario 3 — The Cafeteria Order Chain (Class)
Teacher plays the cafeteria server. Each student orders something — BUT must use a DIFFERENT phrase each time. No repeating: "Can I get…" / "I'd like…" / "Can I have…" / "I need…" / "Do you have…?" — rotate around the class. No one can use a phrase already used.
Chain rule: If a student uses a phrase already used — restart from them. Last student standing wins. Teacher adds menu items: coffee, tea, juice, sandwich, salad, rice, chicken, fruit, water, bread.
90s per student · Scenario 1 · Badge b2 for zero grammar errors in debate
§3
Relay Round · Build the Chain
Team game · Each student adds one sentence · 5 seconds per person · No repeats
10 min
🔗 Relay 1 — The Skills Inventory
Your new manager says: "Tell me what your team can do." Each student adds one CAN sentence. No repeating skills. Build the longest chain possible.
Starter: "I can use Excel and organize data."
Student 2: "I can _______________________________________________"
Student 3: "I can _______________________________________________"
Student 4: "I can _______________________________________________"
Student 5: "But I can't _______________________________________"
Student 6: "However, I can ____________________________________"
📌 Rules: CAN only · No repeated skills · No pause longer than 5 seconds · Repeated skill = restart from that student · Last student must use CAN'T + offer an alternative
🔗 Relay 2 — The Lunch Order
You're ordering lunch for the whole team from the cafeteria. Each student orders something for themselves — using a different request phrase each time AND saying why they like it.
Starter: "Can I get a coffee, please? I like coffee in the morning — it helps me focus."
Student 2: "I'd like ___________ — I like it because ___________"
Student 3: "Can I have _________ — I like ___________________"
Student 4: "I need _____________ — I like ___________________"
Student 5: "I'm not really into ___________ — Can I get _______ instead?"
📌 Each student must: (1) use a different request phrase, (2) say one thing they like about it. "I'm not really into" counts as a special card — only one student can use it.
🔗 Relay 3 — Office Needs Chain
It's Monday morning and the office supply room just opened. Each student says one thing they need — AND one thing a colleague needs. Build a chain of real office needs.
Starter: "I need a charger for my laptop. And Ana needs paper for the printer."
Student 2: "I need __________. And [name] needs __________."
Student 3: "I need __________. And [name] needs __________."
Student 4: "I need __________. And [name] needs __________."
Student 5: "We all need __________ — and our manager needs __________!"
📌 Each student must use NEED twice (I need + [name] needs). No repeating objects. Score: 1 pt per correct NEED sentence. Bonus: 2 pts if student says "Does [name] need a ___?" as a question.
⚡ Teacher Note — Relay Scoring
Track errors on board: GERUND errors ("I like drinking" = ❌), CAN + TO errors ("I can to speak" = ❌), missing 3rd person S ("She need" = ❌). Team with fewest errors gets badge b3. Announce errors publicly — the embarrassment is gentle and productive.
§4
Speed Round · 9 Cards
Click to reveal · Race format · First correct answer scores · Justify for 2 pts
8–10 min
⚡ Teacher Note — Speed Round
Project on screen. Cover the answer — don't click yet. Read situation aloud. First student with hand up: 1 pt for correct sentence, 2 pts if they explain why (can = ability, like = preference, need = requirement). After card 5: no explanations needed — speed only.
Card 01
Your colleague asks: "Do you know how to use the new inventory software?" What's the honest answer about your ability?
✅ CAN: "Yes, I can use it — I learned last week." or "No, I can't yet — can you show me?" Can = ability, honest statement.
Card 02
You arrive at the cafeteria. The server looks at you. You want a black coffee and a chicken sandwich.
✅ ORDERING: "Can I get a black coffee and a chicken sandwich, please?" or "I'd like a coffee and a chicken sandwich, thanks."
Card 03
Your manager asks what you enjoy about your job. Give a real answer using the correct structure — NO gerunds!
✅ LIKE + NOUN: "I like the teamwork and the meetings with clients." ❌ Wrong: "I like working with clients" (gerund = A2.1).
Card 04
A new colleague asks if you can drive to the Salamanca plant. You can — you do it every Thursday.
✅ CAN: "Yes, I can! I drive there every Thursday." Short answer + extra detail = professional and confident.
Card 05
Your desk has no pen, no paper, and no charger. Your laptop is at 4%. What do you say to your colleague?
✅ NEED: "I need a pen, paper, and a charger — fast! My battery is almost dead." Need = urgent requirement. All 3 objects = 3 pts.
Card 06
Someone offers you a soda. You don't like soda. Use the coloquial phrase from S3A — not "I don't like it."
✅ COLLOQUIAL: "I'm not really into soda, thanks — can I get a water instead?" Polite + offers alternative = excellent A1.1 communication.
Card 07
Your manager says "Can you present the data to the Chicago team on Thursday?" It's possible, but you're nervous. What do you say?
✅ CAN + honest: "Yes, I can — but I need the data by Wednesday to prepare." CAN + NEED combined = real professional communication.
Card 08
A client asks "Does your assistant like working with international teams?" — answer for your imaginary assistant.
✅ 3RD PERSON: "Yes, she likes international work — she really likes the variety." LIKES with S for 3rd person. ❌ "She like" = error.
Card 09
⚡ CHALLENGE: Use CAN, LIKE, and NEED all in ONE sentence about your real job.
✅ ALL THREE: "I can manage the team, I like the responsibility, but I need more resources to do it well." One sentence, three structures. Perfect A1.1.
§5
Solo Challenge · The Skills & Cafeteria Pitch
4-minute performance · No notes · All structures · Assessment rubric · Badge b4
12–15 min
📋 Solo Challenge — Official Scenario
You are a new employee at Vertex Logistics in Celaya. It's your first week. Your US manager visits and asks you to lunch in the company cafeteria. During lunch, they ask about your skills and what you like about the job.

You have 4 minutes to complete this role-play — no notes allowed.
1
Order lunch for yourself. Use "Can I get…" or "I'd like…" + say "Anything else?" when prompted. Close with "That's all, thanks."
2
Tell your manager 3 things you CAN do in your role. Be specific — not just "I can work hard."
3
Be honest: say 1 thing you CAN'T do yet — and what you NEED to learn it.
4
Share your preferences: 2 things you LIKE about the job. No gerunds — nouns only.
5
Close strong: ask your manager one question using "Can you…?" or "Do you like…?"
📊 Rubric — Click each when student completes it
CriterionPtsCheck
Ordered using "Can I get…" or "I'd like…" + closed with "That's all, thanks"/ 2Both phrases present
Named 3 specific CAN skills — no generic answers/ 2Each must be a real, specific skill
Used CAN'T honestly + said what they NEED to learn it/ 1CAN'T + NEED in same idea
Used LIKE + noun (no gerund) at least twice/ 1Zero tolerance for "I like working…"
Asked manager a question using CAN or DO YOU LIKE/ 1Initiative = professional bonus
Zero "can + to" errors and zero gerund errors/ 1Grammar accuracy criterion
Spoke for 4 minutes without major stops (>5 seconds)/ 2Fluency — measured by timer
Total: 0 / 10 pts
4 min · No notes · 5 requirements · 10 pts max · Badge b4 on timer end
🎧 Model Monologue — Play AFTER students attempt the solo
Students compare their version to Sofia's. Find every CAN, LIKE, NEED and colloquial phrase she uses.
Sofia's First Lunch at Vertex — Vertex Logistics, Celaya
A1.1 · M5 · S3B · Voice: Grace (ElevenLabs) · Monologue · ≈ 175 words
0:00 / 0:00

SOFIA REYES — VERTEX LOGISTICS — CELAYA · S3B MODEL MONOLOGUE

Hi! I'm Sofia Reyes. It's my first week here at Vertex Logistics in Celaya, and I'm really excited about this job.

Can I get a chicken sandwich and a water, please? That's all, thanks.

So — you want to know about my skills? Sure, no problem! I can use Excel and manage data really well. I can also write reports in English and Spanish. And I can drive — I have my own car, so I can visit the plant in Salamanca too. I can't design graphics yet, but I need to learn that next — maybe a course?

What do I like about the job? I like the team — everyone is very professional. And I like the variety — every day is different. I'm not really into routine work, so this job is perfect for me.

I need a better desk setup — my monitor is a little small! And I need the login for the new inventory system. Can you help me with that?

📎 ElevenLabs · Voice: Grace (Customer Service) · Speed: 0.78 · A1.1 M5 S3B · ≈ 175 words / ≈ 68 sec · Monologue
Sofia uses CAN to describe 3 specific work skills — not just "I can work hard."
Sofia says "I like working with the team" — using a gerund correctly at A1.1.
Sofia uses NEED twice — once for an object and once for something she wants to learn.
Sofia closes her cafeteria order with "That's all, thanks."

§7
Wrap-Up · Certificate & My Win
What you proved · S3 done · S4A is next · Certificate of fluency
5–8 min
01
Production beats knowledge. You didn't just know can/like/need today — you used them under pressure, in debate, timed, solo. That's the gap between learning and speaking. You crossed it.
02
Chunks are power. "Sure, no problem!" / "I'm not really into..." / "Can I get a...?" / "That's all, thanks." — these are not phrases to memorize. They are your professional voice in English. Use them this week.
03
S4A is next. Session 4 builds more complex production: longer role-plays, more integrated vocabulary, and a second speaking challenge. Come ready — the bar goes up.
✅ I Can Now…
I can debate and defend a position using can/can't under time pressure.
I can order food and drinks using 3 different request phrases — not just one.
I can do a 4-minute professional conversation using can, like, and need without notes.
I can use "I'm not really into..." and "Sure, no problem!" naturally in context.
I can explain the difference between can (ability) and like + noun (preference) to someone else.
